title: dedicated: correct backpressure attribution and smoothed utilization reporting for autoscaler
author: Alex Chen
description: Motivation: dedicated fleets were observing spikes in queue length during short-lived bursts; the autoscaler overreacted because utilization was measured without compensating for backpressure and transient tokenbucket bursts. This PR introduces: 1) corrected backpressure attribution so requests that were shed or delayed due to upstream tokenbucket/backpressure are tagged and not counted as successful utilization; 2) a smoothed utilization metric (EMA window configurable) published to the fleet telemetry pipeline used by the dedicated autoscaler; 3) a 'burst_headroom' config parameter and telemetry label that lets the autoscaler distinguish short tokenbucket bursts from sustained demand; 4) dashboard and alerting updates to surface backpressure incidents and corrected utilization; 5) end-to-end tests and integration test harness updates for burst scenarios. Changes were implemented to minimize rollout risk: new metrics are exposed under new names (no breaking rename), autoscaler reads the new metric only when the feature flag is enabled, and defaults preserve current behavior. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for metrics aggregation and tagging - [x] integration tests for burst + backpressure scenario - [x] e2e canary on staging for 48h - [x] docs and runbook updates - [x] load test results attached (see commits) See commits for details and a summary of changed files.

release_notes: Improved dedicated autoscaler stability: backpressure-corrected utilization prevents over-scaling during short-lived tokenbucket bursts; configuration added: smoothed_utilization_ema_window (default: 60s) and burst_headroom (default: 0.15). Dashboard and runbook updated.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated behind feature flag 'dedicated_backpressure_reporting'. Gradual rollout recommended: enable for one small fleet for 24h, then 25% of fleets for 48h before global rollout. If unexpected scale-downs occur, toggle flag off and revert to previous autoscaler config.
